items.title: George "Pops" Foster and Mugsy Spanier Interview, 1957-04-21
items.q: They had a guy they called Kid Punch. We saw him in New Orleans.

ctx.x: How did all that solo business get started? I'll be darn fine, though. I don't know. I guess the public started demanding. When musicians get stars like that, everybody gets a star. I think they had to get a name.

I think Louis and Joe started that round there, because they played all them big numbers like Snaggit and- Yeah, they played the duets. Yeah. And one trumpet they wanted to play, they wanted to be outstanding by themselves. They had a guy they called Kid Punch. We saw him in New Orleans. Well everything he wanted to play, he wanted to make his endings like Louis. Oh, he's got power if he just knows his horn. He's still playing? He's got power if he just knows his horn. Sounds like power.
Oh yeah, we saw a punch coming. He's got the power. But he don't know his horn. You don't know him, huh? No. You know Guy Kelly? He sounds like- You remember Guy Kelly?

items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1959-09-25
items.q: Now, in Chicago you named several fellas that used to sit in with you, white guys. Do you remember Muggsy Spaniel? Oh sure.

ctx.x: I ain't that little boy what you hear I'm talking about now, on drums with me. He was tying it up then. Chani. Chani was a whopping good little drummer then. That boy could play some drum. But he just was always wild, you know. But he always listened to me. He got bad after I left, you know, after I cut out and left, then he turned out bad, you know. But I could tell him, I said, Chani, we're going up to Audubon to play tonight or something like that. I said, we're not going up there drinking. We're going to go…
Now, in Chicago you named several fellas that used to sit in with you, white guys. Do you remember Muggsy Spaniel? Oh sure.

Every weekend we'd do breakfast dance there, you know. And a lot of white boys come up there, gangs of them. You know, they used to come in, sit down, blowin' all of them. Limpinico, Louis Primo. All them fellas used to come up there. Louis Primo was very young then though. He was kind of a young kid, you know.
